children: Gold prices fall despite lower oil prices, as a stronger dollar and rate-hike expectations weigh on the precious metal. In early U.S. trade, New York futures are down 0.3% to $4,385.60 a troy ounce, on track for a weekly loss of 0.5%. Goldman Sachs analysts, however, maintain their gold-price forecast to $5,400 an ounce by the end of next year. "While higher rates should continue to weigh on gold prices through ETF demand in the near term, our economists expect the Fed to deliver three cuts between September 2027 and March 2028, leaving the terminal forecast unchanged at 3.25%-3.5%," they say. "We therefore expect the impact of tighter monetary policy to be felt primarily through a slower near-term appreciation path rather than a lower terminal gold price." (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
